articles.title: 5 ‘lost’ baby orangutans found in Odisha forest
articles.summary: WCCB probes discovery of five infant orangutans in Odisha’s Balasore forest; suspected international trafficking. Rescued apes moved to Nandankanan Zoo.
articles.body: BHUBANESWAR: Five juvenile orangutans, native to Southeast Asia and never recorded in the wild anywhere in India, were found abandoned Tuesday morning in a casuarina forest off NH-16 in Odisha’s Balasore district.Forest officials suspect a transoceanic trafficking network smuggled the apes, all less than a year old, into India and abandoned them near Badipada, in Chandaneswar, after realising they might be caught.Villagers spotted the orangutans dangling from tree branches inside the Bhogarai forest, about 40 km from the Balasore-Kolkata stretch of NH-16, and alerted the forest department.“Our field personnel visited the site and were surprised to discover that all five were baby orangutans, two of them females. As a crowd started gathering near the forest, we decided to bring a cage and safely secure the animals without using tranquillisers,” Balasore divisional forest officer Prateek Indalkar said.“The orangutans were extremely calm. Our team picked up the animals and placed them inside the cage without any difficulty.”Indalkar said the animals might have been transported by road from Kolkata. “Since orangutans are not available in India, we suspect they came from Malaysia to Kolkata by ship.The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) has the expertise to determine the exact species and identify the country from which they originated.”Chief wildlife warden Prem Kumar Jha said orangutans are easy prey for traffickers and are kept illegally as exotic pets by wealthy collectors in several countries.“Whether the animals were being taken to Kolkata for sale to affluent buyers or being moved to another destination will be established soon,” he said.A WCCB team is travelling to Balasore to investigate the animals’ origin. State forest minister Ganesh Ram Singhkhuntia said the probe would go into “how the animals landed in Balasore and from where they were brought since they are not available in India in their natural habitat”.After a medical examination, the rescued orangutans were shifted to the animal rescue centre at Bhubaneswar’s Nandankanan Zoological Park.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha’s name added to Delhi voter list; AAP questions procedure
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha MP from Punjab Raghav Chadha's name has been added to the Delhi electoral rolls currently being revised under the ongoing S.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP Rajya Sabha MP from Punjab Raghav Chadha's name has been added to the Delhi electoral rolls currently being revised under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), poll officials said on Tuesday.The development was raised by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders at a press conference, where they alleged that Chadha's name had been included in the electoral roll of the Rajinder Nagar Assembly constituency without following due procedure, news agency PTI reported.Poll officials, however, said Chadha's name was added to the Delhi electoral rolls through the updation process.His name was removed from the electoral rolls of Punjab, from where he was elected to the Rajya Sabha by his former party, AAP."A total of 700 forms for inclusion of names in the electoral rolls were approval by the electoral registration officers (EROs) in 70 Assembly constituencies in Delhi till Tuesday. Chadha's name was among them," an official at the office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer said.The Delhi electoral roll was frozen on June 16 for preparation of the SIR and remained frozen until August 31, when the draft electoral rolls were published, according to a statement issued by the Delhi CEO's office, PTI reported.During this period, around 2.14 lakh Form-6 applications for new voters, apart from Forms 7 and 8, were submitted by electors.During the claims and objections period, another 25,011 Form-6 applications were submitted in eight days till September 7 for inclusion of names in the final electoral rolls, the statement said.All Form-6 applications submitted for inclusion of names during the pre-SIR period or the claims and objections period are being processed along with Forms 7 and 8.Once the forms are approved, additions, deletions and modifications will be reflected in the electoral database, as applicable, it said.The Delhi CEO's office said additions of electors would be published as a supplementary list on November 4.The AAP questioned how Chadha's name was added to the draft electoral roll after the list for the concerned polling part showed 746 voters.The party sought an explanation from the Election Commission regarding the procedure followed, PTI reported.AAP Delhi unit chief Saurabh Bharadwaj said Chadha's name appeared as the 747th voter in the Rajinder Nagar electoral roll, despite the draft roll published on August 31 showing 746 voters.Bharadwaj said the entry showed the name of Raghav Chadha, son of Sunil Chadha, aged 37, with serial number 747 in the electoral roll of the area.He questioned how the additional entry was made and said the Election Commission should clarify the procedure followed for adding Chadha's articles.title: Delhi building collapse: Already dealt a bad hand, 2 workers meet untimely end
articles.summary: Delhi building collapse at Satya Niketan PG kills welder Paramlal Kori and Surender Singh; DU student Abhishek’s family donates his eyes, seeks accountability.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Paramlal Kori, 30,was the sole breadwinner of his family, living in a rented room in Humayunpur, Safdarjung Enclave, with his wife Vandana and their five-year-old son. He had recently enrolled his son in Class I at a govt school, hoping to secure a better future for him.Paramlal had worked at the Satya Niketan PG facility for only four days when the disaster unfolded Sunday afternoon.That morning, he left for work around 8.30am as usual, carrying lunch packed by Vandana. When he failed to return home that night, a frantic Vandana repeatedly called his phone, only to find it switched off.The following morning, she rushed to the collapse site, clutching a photograph of her husband and pleading for information.By afternoon, her worst fears were confirmed when officials informed the family that Paramlal had died in the collapse, leaving his wife and young son without any source of income.“My husband died under the rubble… Our future looks bleak now. I hope govt helps us with compensation,” Vandana said, adding, “I will work now to raise my son.”A native of Madhya Pradesh, Paramlal moved to Delhi with his family in search of work. He had been living in the city for nearly 20 years, finding odd jobs as a welder. His brother Mukesh said Paramlal earned about Rs 1,200 a day.On Tuesday, Paramlal’s body was taken to his native village in Madhya Pradesh, where his last rites were performed.The tragedy also claimed the life of 56-year-old Surender Singh, who lived with his wife, son and daughter in Arjan Nagar.Tejpal, who worked with him, said Surender was a “calm and quiet man” who had been working as a welder for several years. “He never had a fight with anyone. He kept to himself and was focused on his work,” Tejpal said.After learning about the collapse, Tejpal went to the site with Paramlal’s wife Vandana to search for the two men. They were later told that the injured had been taken to a hospital. The two then rushed there, only to receive the devastating news about their deaths.Mukesh said he had also earlier worked under Surender, who used to take up contracts. Surender’s son was also an earning member of the family and worked elsewhere.Amid the overwhelming grief, the family of DU student Abhishek, who also died in the collapse, found a way to give others a chance at life by donating his eyes.Speaking to media, his father urged govt to take strict action and ensure such a tragedy is not repeated. “Those responsible should be held accountable so that no other family has to suffer a similar loss,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Delhi building collapse: Stuck under rubble, student sent live location to friends
articles.summary: Delhi Satya Niketan PG collapse: 19-year-old DU student sent live location while trapped; rescued by NDRF after 3 hours. Seven dead, five injured.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It had been a hectic few weeks for 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa, who had been campaigning for the upcoming Dusu election and camping with NSUI candidate Vir Chitrath for the past 20 days.On Sunday, as rain forced them to shelve all plans, Neeraj finally returned to Satya Niketan’s Hostel Daze PG. He had just entered his room when suddenly, the walls around him came crashing down.Stuck under a mountain of rubble, he called his friends with a desperate plea: “Bhaiya, please save me. I’ll die here.”A few minutes later, their phone rang again. Neeraj had sent his live location, hoping his friends would come and pull him out soon. Vishnu, one of the boys who reached the site, recounted the frantic search for their friend.“We started to clear debris at the spot where the map located him when, surprisingly, a phone was thrown from a small opening in the rubble.” The lock screen confirmed it was Neeraj’s phone.“Then people started screaming that the adjacent building was also about to collapse, and we ran for our lives. Police didn’t let us go inside again, even though we pleaded that our friend was stuck there,” he said.Neeraj was rescued three hours later, when an NDRF response team pulled him out from the same spot where he had been located by his friends.Back at his home in Jammu’s Kathua, Neeraj’s family had been constantly calling him after hearing that a building had collapsed in Satya Niketan.“Neeraj’s sister, who was watching live coverage of the collapse on TV, recognised the rakhi on his hand as he was taken out. That was when we realised it was his PG that had fallen, and that he was injured,” said Ashok Kumar, a relative.After being pulled out, Neeraj was operated upon at AIIMS Trauma Centre Sunday. On Tuesday, Neeraj underwent a second surgery and remains in a critical condition, according to his family.The teenager had come to Delhi two years ago to pursue a commerce degree from Motilal Nehru College in DU’s South Campus. There he met Nishant Chib, who was also from Jammu, and they became good friends.Neeraj and Nishant moved into different rooms in Hostel Daze PG, but “they would sit together all day in each other’s rooms. It was as if they were roommates,” said Divvy, a mutual friend of theirs.The boys were sitting together Sunday afternoon when their PG collapsed. Nishant told his mother, Seema, that they were separated only by a block of concrete and he could hear Neeraj’s urgent cry for help.Nishant was rescued a few minutes before Neeraj with a head injury. He is currently receiving treatment at AIIMS and is in a stable condition.Locals said the PG, which crumbled like a stack of cards, was one of the most expensive ones in Satya Niketan. According to their friends, Neeraj and Nishant were paying around Rs 15,000 each for a bed in the building.While seven people died in the collapse, five others were injured, two of whom are critical.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: ‘We want justice, not revenge’: Manipur CM, guitarist’s wife seek fair probe, action against accused
articles.summary: Wife seeks justice after Manipur guitarist Chongtham Vikram Singh dies following alleged assault in Delhi; CM urges time-bound probe and NE safety measures.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Joshna Chongtham, wife of Manipuri guitarist Chongtham Vikram Singh who died Monday following an assault allegedly by a group of men, has demanded a fair and impartial investigation into her husband’s death and urged authorities to hold all those responsible accountable under the law.Addressing a news conference in Chanakyapuri Tuesday, she said the family had been devastated by Singh’s death. “I have lost my husband and my son has lost his father. My husband was a peace-loving musician who lived a peaceful life.On Sept 6, around 11.30pm, my husband went downstairs. He came running back upstairs, chased by eight men who beat him up before fleeing,” she said.According to Joshna, 55-year-old Singh complained of breathlessness, following which the family rushed him to the emergency department of Holy Family Hospital. “His blood pressure was found to be very low and, around 6am, he passed away.”Condemning the “senseless and brutal” killing, Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh said in Imphal that the incident was a painful reminder of the safety concerns faced by people from the Northeast living, studying and working in the national capital.In a letter to his Delhi counterpart, Rekha Gupta, Singh urged a fair, time-bound and high-level probe under senior police officers’ supervision, and the prosecution of the accused to the fullest extent of the law. Police said an investigation from all angles was being conducted.He also sought reinforced security measures in localities with significant populations of students and working professionals from northeastern states, stressing that such incidents must not be treated as isolated cases.Thanking everyone for the love and support, Joshna urged the authorities to hold everyone responsible accountable under the law. “We are not seeking revenge. We are seeking justice,” she said. Joshna works at an MNC, while their son is a law student.Binalakshmi Nepram, a founder member of Manipur Women Gun Survivors Network, said, “He lost his life because eight people in Sunlight Colony went up to the third floor and beat him to death in front of his wife and son. Is this the India that we want to live in?”She alleged that the assault was a case of racial violence, emphasising that such attacks must end.Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, who met the family Tuesday, said the killing was a “horrifying incident”, but had no racial angle. He appealed to opposition parties not to indulge in “dirty politics”. “All of Delhi stands with the bereaved family,” the East Delhi MP said.He said Delhi Police, which had already arrested all the accused, would present the chargesheet in court at the earliest. Malhotra also said Delhi govt would recommend that the case be tried expeditiously in a special court.Singh’s son, Yaiphaba, has told police that he was at home when he heard his father shouting. On opening the door, he allegedly saw a group of men kicking and punching Singh. Yaiphaba raised an alarm, following which they fled.He told police that he had seen their faces and would be able to identify them.Singh was then taken to hospital in a taxi by his son, wife and a neighbour. During the journey, Singh told them that the attackers had come from the dhaba opposite their house.He also said some of the men earlier threatened him after he had objected to noise and commotion in the area, Yaiphaba stated.Singh’s neighbour said the family had been living on the third floor with his wife and son for around nine years. “It was close to midnight when I finished dinner and my daughter and I were getting ready for bed. articles.title: PM event arrest: CCTV used to track vehicle, nab youth at his Mumbai home
articles.summary: Mumbai Police arrested Khar resident Rohan Parikh and ex-Army guard Dilip Kunde for using a fake PMO ID to enter BKC’s Jio World Plaza; gun seized.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A day before Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s event at Jio World Plaza in BKC, the city police on Monday arrested a 24-year-old Khar resident and his private security guard, an ex-Army serviceman, for entering the premises claiming to be associated with Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). A third person accompanying them managed to flee.The arrested persons have been identified as Khar resident Rohan Parikh, a science graduate, and his security guard Dilip Kunde. The third accused, Worli’s Prathamesh Bagul (26), is on the run.According to the remand application submitted to the court, Kunde was carrying a firearm when the mall’s security personnel stopped them from entering.Parikh allegedly then showed his identity card, claiming to be from PMO, following which the three were allowed inside.Parikh’s lawyers submitted that he might himself have been duped into believing that he was working for the Prime Minister’s Office. He told the police that he suspected the email sender could be fake. They said Parikh had told earlier the police that his PMO identity card was genuine and he was working as a scientist on confidential research after being appointed by a senior PMO official whose identity, he claimed, could not be disclosed at this stage.Public prosecutor Kranti Kumbhar opposed the plea, maintaining that the PMO identity card was fake and that investigators needed custody to determine how it was procured and the motive behind it.The security staff subsequently alerted BKC police after senior officers received information about the trio. Police examined the CCTV footage and traced the vehicle used by them. Investigators identified Parikh using the vehicle registration and mobile number details and subsequently went to his Khar residence, where he was arrested. During questioning, Parikh allegedly identified Kunde and Bagul as the two men accompanying him.The matter was subsequently handed over to Crime Intelligence Unit (CIU). Police have invoked provisions relating to impersonation, forgery and use of forged documents, alleging that Parikh used a fabricated PMO identity card to gain entry into the premises.On Tuesday, CIU senior inspector Milind Kaate produced Parikh and Kunde before the 37th Metropolitan Magistrate, Mumbai, seeking their police custody. The prosecution sought four days of custody, saying they needed to establish where the alleged fake PMO identity card was obtained, who prepared it and the motive behind the accused allegedly attempting to gain entry into the premises.The court was told that the identity card allegedly shown by Parikh did not mention the designation of the issuing officer. It carried an issue date but no expiry date. Police have seized the card.Police also seized a revolver from Kunde. Police are examining the source and legality of the firearm. A mobile phone has also been seized from the accused. Investigators plan to extract its contents and examine calls, messages and other electronic communications to establish the alleged conspiracy and determine the respective roles of the three men.During preliminary questioning, Kunde allegedly told the police that he had been working as Parikh’s private security guard for around a year and was being paid Rs 1.20 lakh per month. Kunde, who hails from Nashik, is a former Army serviceman.Parikh’s lawyers Anandini Fernandes and Namita Maneshinde told the court that their client had gone to the mall privately to purchase a perfume and denied that he had any connection with Prime Minister’s visit. The defence claimed Parikh had engaged private security from Dec 2025 after allegedly receiving threats from unknown persons.Magistrate D S Khedekar remanded both accused to police custody till Sept 11. In its order, the court noted that the presence of the accused in an area associated with Prime Minister’s programme, coupled with the recovery of a firearm from the guard in the restricted premises, warranted further interrogation.The court observed that the investigation had progressed with the seizure of the identity card and firearm, but custodial interrogation was required to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident.Parikh is reportedly involved in share trading. His uncle, Amal Parikh, is involved in supplying digital chips used in the manufacture of drones.Parikh’s parents and uncle were present in court during the proceedings but declined to speak to the media.Meanwhile, advocate Satish Maneshinde, on behalf of Parikh, issued a statement saying that the allegations concerned a sensitive subject and that a response would be issued after due verification and investigation. articles.title: 'Paid Rs 1.10 lakh to accomplices: Wife, lover held for killing husband in UP
articles.summary: Siddharthnagar police arrest wife, alleged lover and two others for murdering Harishchandra, staging death as e-rickshaw accident; weapon recovered.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Siddharthnagar police claimed to have cracked the sensational murder of a man by arresting four accused, including the victim’s wife and her alleged lover, for allegedly conspiring to murder a man and disguise the crime as an e-rickshaw accident.Police said Harishchandra (35), a resident of Kapiyawa village under Itwa police station limits, was allegedly killed as part of a conspiracy hatched by his wife, Maya Devi, and her alleged lover, Niyaz Ahmad, over an extramarital relationship and ongoing domestic disputes. Investigators alleged that Niyaz paid Rs 1.10 lakh to hired accomplices to execute the murder.According to police, the accused lured Harishchandra to Muhchorwa Ghat on the night of Aug 30 and allegedly stabbed him to death. To cover up the crime, they threw his body into the Budhi Rapti river and positioned his e-rickshaw near the riverbank to create the impression that he had accidentally driven into the water.The murder initially appeared to be an accident until investigators uncovered evidence pointing to a planned killing based on the post-mortem.Later, on the basis of technical evidence, interrogation of suspects and recovery of the murder weapon, police arrested Irshad, Abdullah, Niyaz Ahmad and later Maya Devi.SP Abhishek Mahajan said the investigation revealed that Maya Devi and Niyaz Ahmad were allegedly involved in a relationship and had conspired to eliminate Harishchandra. articles.title: Sharia courts have no legal authority to issue divorce decrees: Chhattisgarh HC
articles.summary: RAIPUR: The Chhattisgarh HC has held that self-styled Sharia courts or religious bodies possess no statutory authority to adjudicate civil or matrimon.
articles.body: RAIPUR: The Chhattisgarh HC has held that self-styled Sharia courts or religious bodies possess no statutory authority to adjudicate civil or matrimonial disputes or alter the legal rights and marital status of citizens.Citing Supreme Court precedents, the bench stated that while religious opinion may guide personal faith, no private institution can assume the authority of a legally established court.The court Monday ruled that decisions or fatwas issued by such informal forums carry no legal weight and cannot be enforced through coercive means.A single bench of Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad passed the order while partially allowing a writ petition filed by a Muslim woman, a resident of Raipur. The petitioner had challenged an order dated Jan 18, 2022, issued by the 'Idara-e-Sharia Islami court' in Raipur, which purported to declare her marriage dissolved after her husband, Mohd Abid Khan, pronounced triple talaq.The petitioner contended that private entities cannot assume judicial powers vested in courts established under the Constitution. She submitted that despite lodging complaints of harassment and setting the law in motion, the religious body issued a declaration affecting her marital status without giving her a chance to be heard.The state govt submitted that the Indian constitutional framework does not recognise any parallel judicial system based on religion. It argued that informal bodies styling themselves as Sharia courts or Darul Qaza (Islamic arbitration and counselling centre) lack statutory recognition and function at best as informal conciliation cells.Justice Prasad declared the order issued by the 'Idara-e-Sharia Islami court'' without legal authority and held that the religious body holds no jurisdiction to pass binding adjudications on matrimonial rights.The HC refrained from adjudicating on the constitutional validity of Talaq-e-Hasan, noting that the larger issue remains pending before the Supreme Court.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Raipur | Silver Rate in Raipur | Bank Holidays in Raipur | Public Holidays in Raipur | Raipur AQI | Weather in Raipur | Petrol Price in Raipur | Diesel Price in Raipur | CNG Price in Raipur | LPG Price in RaipurStay updated with the latest Raipur news. articles.title: US returnee beats father to death: How row over money turned deadly
articles.summary: AHMEDABAD: A dispute over money between an estranged couple turned deadly in Kalol when their son, who had returned from the US six months ago, allege.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: A dispute over money between an estranged couple turned deadly in Kalol when their son, who had returned from the US six months ago, allegedly beat his father to death with a wooden stick.Police said Kalpesh Prajapati, 40, went to confront his father, Kantilal, after the latter allegedly assaulted Kalpesh’s mother during the dispute on Tuesday.The confrontation turned violent, with Kalpesh allegedly attacking him until he collapsed and later died. Kalpesh was traced and arrested in Kalol town in the evening.Family had been living separately for 16 yearsAccording to Kalol City police, Kalpesh lived with his mother, Madhu, 60, at Sankalp Residency near Sudarshan Crossroads. His wife and two daughters live in the US, while he returned to India around six months ago.His father had been living separately for around 16 years and ran a cycle puncture stall near Kapiraj Shopping Centre.Father allegedly assaulted mother over moneyPolice said the trouble began around 10.15am on Tuesday when Kantilal allegedly went near Madhu’s residence carrying a wooden stick and demanded money from her. A quarrel broke out, during which he allegedly abused her and hit her on the leg with the stick.Madhu then called Kalpesh and asked him to speak to his father. According to her complaint, Kalpesh went to Kantilal’s stall around 11.15am to reason with him. However, the conversation allegedly turned into a heated argument.Son allegedly returned to attack fatherPolice said Kalpesh later returned home and told his mother that Kantilal had abused him and refused to listen. He then allegedly returned to the stall, picked up a wooden stick lying nearby and assaulted his father on the head and body.Kantilal suffered serious injuries and collapsed. articles.title: Not just Nepal: How climate change puts European Alps under threat of glacial retreat and rock fall
articles.summary: Europe News: Climate change is increasingly becoming a threat to the snow-clad European Alps, amid initial investigations associating the August 26 Nepal tragedy w.
articles.body: Climate change is increasingly becoming a threat to the snow-clad European Alps, amid initial investigations associating the August 26 Nepal tragedy with rising temperatures.Average temperatures in July, on the Aiguille du Midi peak, in the Mont Blanc range, have more than doubled, from 1.6 C in 1994 to 3.3 C, according to Meteo France, the national weather service.In Lombardy, Italy, Alpine glaciers have reportedly lost more than 40 per cent of their surface area since 1991, according to the region's glacier service.Europe's record heat waves this summer have also affected the permafrost that has held parts of the Alpine landscape together for thousands of years. As the frozen ground thaws, cliffs have become more unstable, triggering rock falls from high elevations.“From mid-July onward, we saw an increase in rock falls. We saw areas becoming difficult to access because of glacial retreat and snowmelt on the glaciers, with crevasses opening up and rock collapses making some areas difficult to reach or traverse”, said Stéphane Bozon, deputy mayor in Chamonix-Mont-Blanc, which shares a border with Italy.Bozon, who oversees safety in Chamonix, told AP that the town needs to prepare urgently for “serious scenarios” in which parts of glaciers or mountains could potentially fall towards inhabited areas.“While it used to snow at high altitudes in the past, now it rains”, said Vanda Bonardo, head of the Italian branch of the International Commission for the Protection of the Alps, a non-governmental organisation.“So we’ve also seen the effects on the stability of the terrain”, she said.Rock falls in the Mont Blanc area have reportedly surged as the permafrost that helps bind the steep Alpine rock faces together has been affected by repeated heat waves.“That doesn't mean that all the rock faces will collapse in the coming years or decades, but quite a number of them are on the verge of becoming unstable and remain stable today only because of the presence of that ice. As the ice changes, we have seen a huge, huge number of rock falls and rock collapses this year”, said Ludovic Ravanel, a researcher at Savoie Mont Blanc University.A collapse is defined as a fall involving more than 100 cubic metres of rock. Ravanel expects the number of such collapses in the Mont Blanc massif this year to “probably reach around 400”. He said this would be about 10 times the level recorded two decades ago.The previous year when conditions came close to this level was 2022, which Ravanel described as the “catastrophic year”, when nearly 300 collapses were recorded.“This has really been one of the defining features of the summer of 2026”, he said.Contains inputs from the Associated Press.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: AHMEDABAD: A 22-year-old woman from Sarkhej, Sofia Farooq, was allegedly killed by her father and brother in the name of “honour” after a video of her with her male friend went viral around three months ago.The accused have been identified as Mohammed Farooq Nawabkhan, 56, and Habil Farooq, 38, said M Division traffic police inspector U B Dhakada.Police said the two, who run a fabrication business, allegedly took Sofia to an isolated stretch near Gheljipura in Sarkhej and attacked her with a hammer before staging the killing as a road accident. Sofia worked as a receptionist at a hospital in Juhapura.It initially appeared to be a hit-and-run case. Police were told that Sofia was riding pillion with Habil on the night of Aug 12 when an unidentified vehicle rammed their motorcycle from behind near Samruddh Dairy.She suffered serious injuries to the back of her head and legs and was taken to Sola Civil Hospital, where she was declared dead on Aug 13.“Investigation revealed that the accident story was fabricated to mislead police,” Dhakada said.Police later found that the accused had allegedly taken Sofia on a motorcycle to an isolated area near Gheljipura village. Police said Habil had concealed an iron hammer in his trousers.“The video involving Sofia and a youth had gone viral around three months earlier, after which her father and brother reprimanded her and objected to her continued conversations with other boys,” Dhakada said.The duo allegedly developed a grudge against Sofia and planned her murder, claiming they wanted to preserve the family’s reputation in their community.Police alleged that after reaching the isolated location, Habil struck Sofia on the head thrice with the hammer, while Farooq assisted him.She was then taken to a public road, where the accused created the impression that an unknown vehicle had hit the motorcycle. “The accused lodged a false complaint about an unknown vehicle and created a fake accident narrative to mislead the investigation,” Dhakada said.A case has been registered for murder against the father-son duo.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: Survival instinct: From under rubble, student sent live location to friends
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: It had been a hectic few weeks for 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa, who had been campaigning for the upcoming DUSU election and camping with NSUI c.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: It had been a hectic few weeks for 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa, who had been campaigning for the upcoming DUSU election and camping with NSUI candidate Virr Chatrath for the past 20 days.On Sunday, as rain forced them to shelve all plans, Neeraj finally returned to Satya Niketan’s Hostel Daze PG. He had just entered his room when suddenly, the walls around him came crashing down. Stuck under a mountain of rubble, he called his friends with a desperate plea: “Bhaiya, please save me. I’ll die here.”A few minutes later, their phone rang again. Neeraj had sent his live location, hoping his friends would come and pull him out soon. Vishnu, one of the boys who reached the site, recounted the frantic search for their friend.“We started to clear debris at the spot where the map located him when, surprisingly, a phone was thrown from a small opening in the rubble.” The lock screen confirmed it was Neeraj’s phone.“Then people started screaming that the adjacent building was also about to collapse, and we ran for our lives. Police didn’t let us go inside again, even though we pleaded that our friend was stuck there,” he said.Neeraj was rescued three hours later, when an NDRF response team pulled him out from the same spot where he had been located by his friends.Back at his home in Jammu’s Kathua, Neeraj’s family had been constantly calling him after hearing that a building had collapsed in Satya Niketan.“Neeraj’s sister, who was watching live coverage of the collapse on TV, recognised the rakhi on his hand as he was taken out. That was when we realised it was his PG that had fallen, and that he was injured,” said Ashok Kumar, a relative.After being pulled out, Neeraj was operated upon at AIIMS Trauma Centre Sunday. On Tuesday, Neeraj underwent a second surgery and remains in a critical condition, according to his family.The teenager had come to Delhi two years ago to pursue a commerce degree from Motilal Nehru College in DU’s South Campus. There he met Nitish Chib, who was also from Jammu, and they became good friends. Neeraj and Nitish moved into different rooms in Hostel Daze PG, but “they would sit together all day in each other’s rooms. It was as if they were roommates,” said Divvy, a mutual friend of theirs.The boys were sitting together Sunday afternoon when their PG collapsed. Nitish told his mother, Seema, that they were separated only by a block of concrete and he could hear Neeraj’s urgent cry for help. Nitish was rescued a few minutes before Neeraj with a head injury. He is currently receiving treatment at AIIMS and is in a stable condition.Locals said the PG, which crumbled like a stack of cards, was one of the most expensive ones in Satya Niketan. According to their friends, Neeraj and Nitish were paying around Rs 15,000 each for a bed in the building.While seven people died in the collapse, five others were injured, two of whom are critical.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: World's highest-paid Prime Minister gets salary hike of 9%; pledges to donate difference to charity
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Singapore’s ministers, who are among the world’s highest-paid government officials, are set to receive their first salary increase in 15 years. Prime .
articles.body: Singapore’s ministers, who are among the world’s highest-paid government officials, are set to receive their first salary increase in 15 years. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has justified the increase in pay by stating that it is necessary to attract top talent into politics.Under the revised framework, the benchmark annual salary for a minister at the lowest grade will rise to S$1.8 million (approx Rs 13.5 crores) from S$1.1 million (approx Rs 8.2 crores). The prime minister’s benchmark will increase to S$3.6 million (approx Rs 27 crores) from S$2.2 million (approx Rs 16.5 crores).The increases will not immediately take ministers to those benchmarks. Instead, they will receive a one-time adjustment of up to 9% from October 15, depending on their performance and responsibilities. Wong said most ministers at the lowest grade are expected to earn about S$1.35 million (approx Rs 10.12 crores) by the end of the current term.Wong did not disclose his own salary but said a 9% increase would take it to about S$2.4 million (approx Rs 18 crores). He added that he would donate his entire salary increase to charity for the next five years.Political pay remains a sensitive issue in Singapore, as ministers tend to earn far more than most citizens. The government has long defended the system stating that it is required to attract capable people from both private sector and public service and to maintain a clean government.Wong said ministerial salaries had increasingly fallen behind comparable earnings in the private sector and civil service, making a review necessary. The new framework uses the median income of Singapore’s top 1,000 citizen earners as a reference, with a 40% discount applied to reflect the nature of political service.The government said the new framework would be reviewed every five years. Singapore’s current political salary system was established after a 2011 review, which resulted in a roughly 36% pay cut following public concerns over political salaries. A 2017 review recommended adjustments that were not implemented, while a review scheduled for 2023 was deferred.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: GUWAHATI: Ramanuj Goswami, accused of beheading his wife and storing her severed head in a refrigerator, on Tuesday said he has no remorse and now plans to kill his wife's 'sugar daddy' next.Goswami made this chilling remark to reporters while being taken for a medical examination."I have no regret and no apology for whatever I did. I've eliminated my wife, and the moment I am out of jail, her sugar daddy is next." He, however, did not identify the person he called his wife's 'sugar daddy'.Police arrested Goswami on Sunday night for allegedly killing his wife, Riya Talukdar, at their flat in Basisthapur in Guwahati's Beltola area on the morning of Sept 3.Investigators recovered Talukdar's severed head, packed in a polythene bag, from a refrigerator inside the flat. A machete, locally known as a 'dao' and allegedly used in the killing, and several liquor bottles were also seized.The couple had married on Sept 22 last year.Goswami was produced before a local court on Monday evening and remanded in police custody for seven days.A police officer said, "The interrogation of the accused is underway. The interrogation so far has revealed that there were frequent arguments between the couple over various issues including the alleged extramarital affair of the deceased, which the accused told the police during interrogation. On Sept 3, they had an argument and the accused lost his temper and committed the crime."The allegation of an extramarital affair was made by Goswami during questioning and has not been independently established.Originally from Gauripur in lower Assam's Dhubri district, Goswami had been living in the Guwahati flat for the past few years.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Meta launches Muse, a personal AI Agent that can do your everyday tasks; company makes a 'promise' after Muse AI Image 'fiasco' that allowed anyone to create AI images with users' Instagram photos
articles.summary: Tech News News: Meta has launched a new autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) assistant capable of executing tasks such as sending emails, listing a car for sale, a.
articles.body: Meta has launched a new autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) assistant capable of executing tasks such as sending emails, listing a car for sale, and booking travel. The system, dubbed "Muse" and known internally as "Hatch," reportedly serves as the cornerstone of CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s ambitions to deliver what he calls "personal superintelligence" across Meta's global platform. In a post on X, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote, "Introducing Muse, the personal agent that understands your goals and works 24/7 to get things done for you."Initially limited to U.S. users, Muse will operate through a standalone app and within Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform. The company that for now, Muse launches on iOS, Android and the web, with free and paid tiers, and support for AI glasses coming soon.Based on the open-source OpenClaw framework, Muse functions by linking directly to a user’s calendar, email, financial services, smart home hardware, and health platforms. Meta noted that users must manually grant permissions for each service and retain the ability to revoke access at any point.Unlike traditional chatbots, each Muse instance runs within an isolated, cloud-based virtual machine designed to emulate an individual personal computer. This architecture allows the software to execute long-running tasks autonomously in the background without requiring continuous user interaction.Incidentally, the Muse AI agent comes despite reported internal concerns regarding how the software handles sensitive personal data. The system’s deep integration with personal data has intensified scrutiny over potential safety, privacy, and operational hazards—particularly the risk of the agent executing erroneous transactions or mismanaging private information.Meta's security promiseMeta has made a strong security promise including claims of implementing additional security safeguards. According to Vishal Shah, the company’s vice president of AI products, the engineering revisions successfully brought the tool in line with Meta's baseline thresholds for privacy, security, and model performance. "It is impossible to say that there is never going to be a mistake, but every single part of the architecture has been designed to make this as safe, as secure, as private as we can possibly make it," Shah said. Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said the app runs within “its own isolated environment” inside the company’s computing infrastructure, and “never sees your actual passwords or payment details.”In July this year, Meta launched a new AI image generator, Meta AI Image, that allowed anyone to create AI images with users' Instagram photos. Also, if users had a public Instagram account, Meta automatically opted them in.Muse comes hours before Apple's Big eventMeta Muse AI assistant arrives just hours before Apple upgrades its voice assistant Siri AI for the chatbot era. While Siri AI is capable of taking some actions, it is not a full blown agentic system yet like OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI and Meta AI offer. Apple is likely to launch it at its September 9 event, along with new iPhones.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: 'Crushing those who question': Rahul Gandhi demands Punjab FM's resignation over Gulzar Singh’s death
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday accused Aam Aadmi Party of \"crushing those who question\" the Punjab government aft.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday accused Aam Aadmi Party of "crushing those who question" the Punjab government after a man died by suicide following alleged pressure to apologise for publicly questioning the state's finance minister over the drug menace in the state.In a social media post on X, Rahul said Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should immediately demand his minister Harpal Singh Cheema's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation."A dangerous pattern is emerging in Punjab's AAP government - if you question government failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said."Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the finance minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologise, that he consumed poison. Wandering from one hospital to another, without access to treatment, he ultimately lost the battle for his life," he added.He said the government's job is to answer to the people, "not to crush those who ask questions"."Last week, I also spoke with a young Mohanjeet Singh, who was tortured for protesting against chief minister Bhagwant Mann," Rahul said."The government's job is to answer to the people, not to crush those who ask questions. May Gulzar Singh ji's family get justice as soon as possible. The chief minister should immediately demand the finance minister's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation, with his name registered in the FIR," he added.A controversy erupted after a 47-year-old man, Gulzar Singh, from Sangrur allegedly died by suicide, with his family claiming that he was asked to apologise and subjected to casteist slurs for questioning finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the "unabated" supply of 'chitta' in his area at an event on September 6.Singh died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison, his family members said.A purported video of Gulzar's last moments surfaced in which he spoke about questioning the finance minister, prompting opposition parties to demand the resignations of Cheema as well as Mann.Punjab Police set up a special investigation team (SIT), led by an officer of additional director general of police rank, in connection with the suicide incident.Following a complaint by Gulzar's family, five villagers - Baljit Singh, Sukhdev Singh, Vicky Singh, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur - have been booked under Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and relevant sections of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, according to the FIR.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Father wins Rs 22,500 after courier company fails to deliver diapers ordered for baby daughter
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Xpressbees to pay Rs 15,000 compensation and Rs 7,500 towards litigation expenses aft.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed Xpressbees to pay Rs 15,000 compensation and Rs 7,500 towards litigation expenses after finding deficiency in service over the repeated failure to deliver a packet of diapers. The commission also ordered the courier company to take corrective measures to ensure delivery attempts are accurately recorded. The order was passed on August 21, 2026.Why did the consumer approach the commission?According to the commission order, the consumer ordered MamyPoko pants diapers worth Rs 1,429 from the FirstCry online platform on March 9, 2025, for his 1.5-year-old daughter. The product was dispatched the same day and reached the Xpressbees hub in Thiruvalla on March 10.The delivery was initially promised for March 12, but the product was not delivered. On March 14, the consumer received an “out for delivery” message naming a delivery agent. However, when he contacted the agent, he was allegedly told that the agent was not assigned to the route and did not have information about the shipment.The consumer then raised complaints with FirstCry and Xpressbees and also approached the National Consumer Helpline. Despite further delivery dates being shown in the system, the consignment was not delivered. On March 24, FirstCry cancelled the order and initiated a refund.The consumer alleged that the shipment had been wrongly marked as refused through OTP-based delivery even though no delivery agent had actually reached his premises. He also said the delay forced him to buy diapers from local shops at a higher price.Xpressbees denied the allegations and said the consumer had refused to provide the OTP needed for delivery. It also attributed the delay to technical allocation errors, workforce constraints and operational difficulties.What did the commission find about the failed delivery?The bench comprising President George Baby and member Nishad Thankappan noted that Xpressbees admitted receiving the shipment and that it had reached the Thiruvalla hub. The company also acknowledged that a delivery attempt was made on March 14, while attributing the failure partly to technical and operational issues.The commission found that the consumer had repeatedly complained about the non-delivery while the shipment was still pending. However, Xpressbees did not produce independent evidence showing that its delivery agent had actually reached the consumer’s premises and that he had refused to provide the OTP.The commission said the courier company had not produced records such as call details, GPS or location data, delivery photographs or doorstep confirmation to support its claim.“The opposite parties 01st and 02nd state that the first attempt failed due to technical allocation errors and refusal of OTP. But the evidence before the commission does not satisfactorily establish that the complainant's alleged refusal was the actual reason for the prolonged non-delivery and eventual return of the shipment,” the commission held.It also rejected the argument that workforce shortages and operational difficulties could completely absolve the courier company, particularly after the shipment had reached the destination hub and repeated complaints had been made.“The contention relating to workforce constraints, resignations, operational contingencies and communication lapses is also insufficient to completely absolve the logistics provider,” the commission said.The commission concluded that the repeated failure to deliver, the admitted technical allocation problem, lack of proof of an actual doorstep OTP refusal and eventual return of the shipment established a shortcoming in the delivery service.“We feel that the repeated failure to effect delivery, the admitted technical allocation problem, the absence of convincing proof of an actual doorstep OTP refusal and the return of the consignment, despite repeated complaints by the complainant, prove a shortcoming in the manner in which the delivery service was performed,” it held.The commission found deficiency in service against the first and second opposite parties and directed them to jointly and severally pay Rs 15,000 compensation for inconvenience, mental agony and loss, along with Rs 7,500 towards litigation expenses.The amounts have to be paid within 30 days of receiving the order, failing which they will carry 9 percent annual interest until realisation.The commission also directed Xpressbees to ensure that delivery-attempt statuses are entered accurately and that a shipment is not marked as refused by a customer unless there has been a genuine delivery attempt supported by a verifiable record.

articles.title: Gene Autry bought a 110-acre California movie ranch in 1952; a massive fire destroyed 54 buildings before he finally sold the last 10 acres
articles.summary: US News: Before Melody Ranch became associated with Gene Autry, it was already part of the machinery of early Hollywood. The Newhall property opened in 1915 as.
articles.body: Before Melody Ranch became associated with Gene Autry, it was already part of the machinery of early Hollywood. The Newhall property opened in 1915 as Monogram Studios, providing a ready-made setting for Western films at a time when the genre was becoming a staple of American cinema. John Wayne was among the performers whose early productions used the site. Autry had filmed there himself before purchasing it in 1952. Under his ownership, the ranch was renamed Melody Ranch and adapted to the demands of television, with several Flying A Pictures series made on its sets.The property later hosted a long list of Western programmes, from Hopalong Cassidy to Gunsmoke. Then a fire swept through Placerita Canyon in 1962. Fifty-four structures were destroyed, along with much of Autry's collection. What followed was not a clean ending, but decades of selling, rebuilding and changing use.Melody Ranch began as a Hollywood Western film studio in 1915The property was already established as a movie location when Gene Autry acquired it. Known as Monogram Studios, the Newhall ranch had opened in 1915, during the formative years of the Western film industry. Its sets were used for early Western productions, including a number of John Wayne's Lone Star Monogram films.Autry himself had a connection to the site before he owned it. His 1935 film Tumbling Tumbleweeds, made for Republic Pictures, was among the productions associated with the ranch.By the time Autry bought the property in 1952, the place had accumulated a useful collection of Western settings. That made it suitable for the new television market, where producers needed locations that could be redressed and reused without building an entire town for every production.Autry renamed the property Melody Ranch and turned much of its attention towards television.Gene Autry turned Melody Ranch into a television Western hubThe ranch became the base for several of Autry's Flying A Pictures productions. The Gene Autry Show was filmed there, as were The Range Rider, Annie Oakley, Buffalo Bill, Jr. and The Adventures of Champion.Other Western series passed through the gates. Hopalong Cassidy, Wild Bill Hickok, Wyatt Earp, The Cisco Kid, Sheriff of Cochise and Gunsmoke all used Melody Ranch at various points. The property was not limited to television either. Feature films continued to use its sets, including Fred MacMurray's At Gunpoint in 1955, as reported.The ranch offered a ready-made Western environment, with streets, buildings and open areas that could serve different productions. Camera crews could find useful angles without having to construct an entirely new setting.Autry also appeared there with Champion, the horse who became one of the most recognisable animals associated with his career. Photographs from the 1950s show the pair on the ranch's Western street.The Melody Ranch fire wiped out much of Autry’s Western collectionFor Autry, Melody Ranch was more than a place where productions could be made. He had accumulated a substantial collection connected with his career, including antique automobiles, stagecoaches, costumes, documents, recordings and other memorabilia. He was considering turning the property into a Western museum.According to the official website of Gene Autry, that plan changed on August 28, 1962. A major fire swept through Placerita Canyon in Newhall and reached the ranch. Fifty-four structures on the 110-acre property were destroyed. The losses extended well beyond the buildings themselves. Autry's collection of vehicles and stagecoaches was badly affected, as were his wardrobe and costumes, papers and other material. An archive containing about 17,000 recordings was also lost.Several parts of the ranch escaped the destruction. The adobe house survived, along with another house, the adobe village, a schoolhouse, a cabin and the main entrance.The fire effectively ended Melody Ranch's period as a large working film and television property under Autry.After the fire, Melody Ranch slowly passed out of Autry’s handsAutry abandoned his plans for a museum and the ranch entered a much quieter period. Over the following three decades, he gradually sold most of the property to developers.The landholding became a fraction of what it had been. The original ranch covered 110 acres; eventually only a small remnant remained in Autry's hands.Champion Three, rather than film production, became an important part of the property's later story. The horse remained at Melody Ranch until his death in 1990. After that, Autry sold the remaining ranch to brothers Renaud and Andre Veluzat.The Veluzat family already had deep connections with film locations in the Santa Clarita Valley. Their family had operated a film ranch in Saugus since the early 1950s, and the brothers took on the task of bringing Melody Ranch back into use.Old photographs helped restore Melody Ranch’s Western streetRestoration meant working from what little remained and from the visual record of the ranch's earlier years. The Veluzats used old photographs and videotapes to reconstruct the Western street and church sets, aiming to recreate their appearance from the early television period.There was one practical alteration. The rebuilt street sits slightly higher than the original version. That change was made for the camera rather than historical accuracy, helping keep the residential development on the hill north of the ranch out of shots.The restored street eventually returned to television production. Among the programmes to use the setting was HBO's Deadwood, giving the old ranch another connection with Western screen history decades after Autry's productions had ended.A museum keeps Melody Ranch’s Hollywood history on displayThe property also retains a museum devoted to its film history. Its collection includes vintage automobiles, photographs, Champion's training hoop and other material from the ranch's years in the entertainment business. Visits are arranged by appointment rather than through ordinary daily opening hours.The surviving site is therefore considerably smaller than the place Autry purchased in 1952. The 110-acre ranch that once accommodated a busy collection of film and television productions was progressively reduced through development and sale, leaving only a small portion of the original property.Yet the surviving sets preserve something of the ranch's working appearance. Buildings that were once scenery for weekly television programmes became historic pieces of a California film landscape.Melody Ranch after the studio yearsMelody Ranch also developed a life outside film production. Since 1994, it has hosted the Santa Clarita Cowboy Poetry and Music Festival each March. The event brings performers, musicians and visitors to the ranch, alongside Western-themed displays, food and merchandise.The ranch's history is unusually layered for a surviving film location. It began in the silent-era and early Hollywood period, became part of Autry's television operation, was heavily damaged by fire, passed out of his ownership and was eventually restored by a family already familiar with the business of maintaining film ranches.What remains is not the 110-acre property Autry bought. It is a much smaller piece of it, shaped by decades of production, fire, development and restoration. The Western street, rebuilt from photographs and old footage, provides the most visible reminder of the ranch's former role. Beneath that scenery is a longer story about how quickly a working Hollywood location can disappear, and how parts of it can still be reconstructed many years later.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 4 floors higher, Rs 4 lakh a month: The greed behind Delhi PG ‘Hostel Daze’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For students and young professionals who leave their hometowns for Delhi in pursuit of their dreams, a paying guest accommodation can gradu.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For students and young professionals who leave their hometowns for Delhi in pursuit of their dreams, a paying guest accommodation can gradually become much more than four walls and a bed.It becomes a second home — where they return after college or work, eat their meals, prepare for exams, attend late-night meetings and call their families before going to sleep.But the collapse of a five-storey building housing a boys' PG in south Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, which claimed seven lives, has shaken that sense of security.For many living in PGs across Delhi-NCR, a question that was once easy to ignore has now become difficult to escape: How safe is the building they call home?Also read: After Satya Niketan PG collapse, CM Rekha Gupta orders bulldozer action across Delhi'Profit over safety'The FIR registered in the case states that building owner Hariram Gupta and his brother constructed four additional floors on top of the old structure to earn more rental income, despite allegedly being aware that the foundation could not bear the additional weight.The building was more than 40 years old. The Gupta family had recently repaired it and converted it into a paying-guest facility, taking advantage of the property's proximity to Delhi University.During interrogation, Mahesh Gupta, who was managing the accommodation on behalf of his parents Hariram and Urmila, said the building had been leased to PG operator ‘Hostel Daze’ in August 2025.Two shops on the ground floor were also being merged and expanded into one, police said.Sources said a load-bearing wall was allegedly removed during the construction, potentially compromising the stability of the building and contributing to its eventual collapse.“Mahesh was questioned about the construction and documents related to its possession and ownership,” a police source said.The property is believed to have been generating more than Rs 4 lakh in revenue each month, according to sources.Investigators are also expected to examine what sources described as the “PG mafia” in the area — private players allegedly facilitating illegal construction and the operation of PGs on commission.Owner apprehended after police raidsDelhi Police said owner Hariram Gupta was apprehended after more than 10 teams were deployed to locate him.Police said Gupta was missing from his Gurgaon home when teams reached there. Technical surveillance was then used to trace his movements, while a look-out circular was issued to prevent him from leaving the country.The investigation is likely to examine not only the construction and ownership of the building but also how it was allowed to operate as a PG.‘What if the building is not safe?’Until now, choosing a PG was largely about rent, food, Wi-Fi and proximity to college or the workplace.The condition of the building, its permissions and approvals, and what would happen in an emergency often remained outside that calculation.For students now living in PGs, the Satya Niketan collapse has changed that.Sneha Mishra, who lives at 'New PG for Girls' in Sant Nagar, said the incident has changed the way she looks at the place she has come to regard as home after moving to Delhi from Deoghar, Jharkhand.“When I came to Delhi from Deoghar, this PG became my second home. I eat, study and sleep here, but I never really thought about whether the place I call home is actually safe,” Mishra told ANI.That thought, she said, now follows her even when she is trying to sleep.“Earlier, I never thought about the condition of the building. Now, when I go to sleep, there is a question in my mind — what if the building we trust with our lives is not safe?” she told ANI.The concern also extends to the families who send their children to Delhi believing they have found a secure place for them to live.“Our parents send us here believing we are safe. After Satya Niketan, many of us have started looking at the roof over our heads differently,” Mishra told ANI.Safety comes with a priceFor many young people, however, finding a safer place is not simply a matter of making a choice. It is also about whether they can afford one.A better-maintained PG can mean higher monthly rent, which can be difficult for students and people earning entry-level salaries. In a city where every extra thousand rupees can matter, safety can end up competing with affordability.Shilpashree Mondal, who lives in a PG in Noida, said her budget leaves little room for choice.“I don’t think even a working woman like me has much of a real choice when it comes to choosing where to live. Budget decides most of it, especially in a city like Delhi, where finding a safe and affordable place can be difficult,” Mondal told ANI.The Satya Niketan collapse initially frightened Mondal. But the fear soon prompted her to take a closer look at the place where she lives.“I started thinking, what if something like this happens to my PG too? I somehow convinced myself that it wouldn’t happen, but there are already things that worry me, like problems with the water supply, poor hygiene and dampness in the walls,” she said.Often, she said, residents discover the real condition of a PG only after moving in.“The owner and caretakers often make things look safer and better than they actually are, but you only realise the real problems once you start living there,” Mondal told ANI.‘I started noticing how my building is designed’For Pallavi Joshi, who hails from Uttarakhand's Haldwani and has lived in a Delhi PG for nearly two years, the collapse has changed an otherwise ordinary nightly routine.“I had never thought about the structure of my PG before. After Satya Niketan, I started noticing how my building is designed and wondering whether there are enough safety measures. Even at night, I sometimes think about what would happen if something went wrong here,” Joshi told ANI.Joshi said neither her PG owner nor anyone from the management approached the residents after the incident to discuss their concerns or reassure them about the safety of the building.She said PG owners often focused on collecting rent on time, while issues such as safety, hygiene and emergency preparedness received less attention.Students want to see the paperworkFor Vijaya Roy, a student at Delhi University's Ramanujan College who is preparing for the CAT examination, the uncertainty begins with something as basic as knowing whether a PG has the necessary permissions.Around 20 to 25 people live in her PG, she told ANI, but residents are not always told whether the property has the required approvals.“We don’t even know whether they have permission from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi or not. When we first come to the PG, they demand documents from us, but they don’t show any papers to us,” Roy told ANI.Roy said students should not have to rely solely on an owner's word when it comes to the building where they sleep every night.“It should be made mandatory that tenants are able to get the papers from PG owners, so that they know whether the building has the proper permissions and whether the regulations are being followed,” she said.For Delhi University students, the shortage of affordable hostel accommodation makes that dependence on PGs even greater, Roy said.“If adequate hostel facilities are available in colleges, students will have another option. PG owners will not have the same monopoly and may be forced to improve conditions,” she told ANI.Delhi government plans PG regulationThe Satya Niketan collapse has also intensified scrutiny of PG accommodation in the capital.The Delhi government is working on a comprehensive policy to regulate paying guest accommodations, with Urban Development Minister Ashish Sood outlining proposed measures aimed at improving safety, security and rent regulation.Under the proposed policy, PG operators would have to obtain a PG Operating Licence and complete police and municipal verification before running their establishments.CCTV cameras would be mandatory at entrances and in common areas, with recordings required to be preserved for 30 days.For PGs housing 15 or more students, operators would have to employ a licensed night guard between 10pm and 6am. Visitor registers would also be mandatory, while non-resident visitors would be allowed entry between 8am and 9pm.Every PG would also be required to have a warden either living on the premises or maintaining an office within a 500-metre radius. The warden would have to be physically available within 15 minutes during an emergency.The proposed policy also seeks to address concerns about arbitrary and high rents through a Rent Regulation Committee, which would determine rent bands for different areas.These rent bands would take into account factors such as occupancy levels, amenities, prevailing market rates and proximity to colleges and public transport.The draft framework further proposes an Institutional Accommodation Committee comprising college officials, student representatives, a municipal representative and a police liaison officer.A second home no longer feels quite as secureFor the students and young professionals living in PGs across Delhi-NCR, the Satya Niketan collapse is no longer simply an incident they watched on a news screen.It has changed how they look at their own rooms — the damp patch on a wall, the makeshift partition, the crowded staircase or the roof above their bed.A PG may still be a second home. But after Satya Niketan, many residents are asking whether the place they depend on for safety is actually capable of providing it.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Nearly 4,000 New York City students planted more than 100,000 beachgrass stalks across 2.25 acres at Coney Island Creek Park to rebuild protective dunes and help protect 50,000+ people from flooding
articles.summary: US News: Nearly 4,000 New York City public school students have taken part in an effort to restore protective dunes at Coney Island Creek Park in Brooklyn. Sin.
articles.body: Nearly 4,000 New York City public school students have taken part in an effort to restore protective dunes at Coney Island Creek Park in Brooklyn. Since 2022, students, teachers and community members have planted more than 100,000 American beachgrass culms across more than 2.25 acres of frontal dunes.The project is part of the Resilient Schools and Communities (RiSC) programme run by the National Wildlife Federation (NWF). According to the organisation, it combines environmental education with habitat restoration and aims to help the local community prepare for flooding and other risks linked to extreme weather.Coney Island’s coastline has faced serious flooding during major storms. Superstorm Sandy in 2012 and Hurricane Ida in 2021 highlighted the risks faced by the area. The RiSC programme was launched in 2017 in seven South Brooklyn public schools, including schools in Coney Island, to help students understand these risks and learn about the environment around them.The programme was also created to address gaps in climate education. At the time, students were receiving limited climate education, mainly through science classes, while resilience was not part of their curriculum. NWF developed a curriculum and a RiSC Vulnerability Assessment to help students understand how their schools and communities could be affected by climate-related risks and how those risks could be addressed.How beachgrass can protect the coastThe restoration work focuses on American beachgrass, a native plant with a dense network of roots and rhizomes. These underground structures help the grass hold soil together. Its ability to stabilise dunes and reduce erosion has been documented, while the dunes can also provide coastal flood protection during extreme wave conditions.The beachgrass also provides cover for wildlife found in Coney Island Creek Park, including snakes, small mammals and native and migratory birds.Since 2022, habitat restoration events at the park have involved students, teachers, volunteers and community members. Nearly 4,000 public school students, more than 200 teachers and hundreds of community members have worked with NWF, NYC Parks, the American Littoral Society, corporate volunteers and Coney Islanders.The planting effort has so far restored more than 2.25 acres of frontal dunes. Teachers are also brought to the site for professional development, connecting the restoration work with environmental education.The programme aims to expand the plantings further, with the goal of building functional flood protection for more than 50,000 people living next to Coney Island Creek Park.The organisation also wants the plantings to help stop sand from moving into roads, homes and sewer drains, as clogged drains can worsen flooding on streets.Lessons from Superstorm SandyThe RiSC programme was shaped by what happened during Superstorm Sandy in October 2012. About 50,000 homes in Coney Island were left uninhabitable after the storm. Thousands of public housing residents were without heat and hot water for weeks, while an 11-foot storm surge brought polluted water and sand into homes and businesses.The RiSC 3.0 curriculum was developed specifically for Coney Island. It was created with community leaders, teachers and scientific advisers and looked at the area’s ecological and social history, as well as its vulnerability to coastal flooding.The programme also draws on the role of dunes in protecting coastal communities. FEMA states that primary frontal dunes are often the first line of defence against flooding in coastal regions.The plan is to continue planting native woody shrubs and trees in the maritime forest near the road. These plantings are expected to provide additional flood protection and sand stabilisation, while also creating more habitat for birds.Coney Island Creek Park has also recorded a wide range of bird species. According to NWF, eBirders have documented 244 species in the park, including grebes, loons, gulls, terns, warblers, ducks and sandpipers.Community support and long-term workCommunity involvement has been central to the project. In November 2025, the organisation carried out extensive outreach in Coney Island before holding a meeting where residents could learn about the RiSC programme, ask questions and provide feedback.The meeting was attended by students, community board members, representatives from four elected officials’ offices and a homeowner association. NWF said feedback towards the programme was overwhelmingly positive, while continued shoreline restoration was identified as a top priority by the local community board.The organisation has built relationships within the Coney Island community since 2020. NYC public schools have continued to support the habitat restoration work, while NYC Parks has helped with permits, staff, tools, plant material and other supplies.Emily Fano, who leads the NYC project for NWF, said the organisation learned that working in a community with a history of disinvestment required patience and trust.“I think about these four key things as a nonprofit coming into a frontline community like Coney Island that has experienced historic disinvestment: listen, be humble, earn trust, and ask what people need,” Fano said.She said residents were involved in programme planning and design as paid advisers, while local educators and volunteers received stipends.The organisation has committed to continuing its work in Coney Island until it is sure that the plantings provide functional flood protection.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
